checks.rule: Names the product or feature and what it was used for.
Names the user role and the concrete task they were completing.
Traces input, processing, storage or integration, and user-visible result.
Names system components by layer and an ordered request flow (for example UI → API → data → AI → response) specific to the point.
Separates the candidate's actions from team or system behavior.
Explains what each named technology did.
Each technology has a version and eraFit consistent with the résumé window and tech landscape timelineChecks.
Names partners such as Product, UX, or adjacent teams and how communication happened.
Uses landscape domain patterns or architecture hooks when the point claims specialized work such as agents.
For experience in 2024 or later, includes a natural AI coding-assistant hint or an explicit reason it does not apply; never force AI tooling into pre-2024 stories.
Separates technical result from business or user impact.
Every numeric claim has before, after, formula, scope, and evidence.
Names at least one failure path and the remedy or prevention when relevant.
Connects the experience to a specific responsibility in the target role.
Avoids unexplained generic claims such as scalable, optimized, robust, or enterprise.
generalAnswers includes every required id from evals/general-questions.json.
Tell me about yourself is about 60 seconds spoken, standard shape, not a full résumé dump.
Intro, why-company, AI workflow, and ask-for-help answers each have a distinct angle.

acceptance: A preparation can be finalized only when structural validation passes and no quality check is marked fail. Review items may remain for candidate confirmation.
